target_customer: Donors who pay utility bills on behalf of low income households in Detroit and Baltimore; beneficiaries are families and seniors at risk of water shutoff. The organization is a nonprofit funded by donations.
problem: Tens of thousands of Detroit households had water service cut off in 2014 over unpaid bills. The Human Utility lets donors pay a specific family's bill directly to the utility.
business_model: 501(c)(3) nonprofit funded by individual donations; donors pay utilities directly

founders.name: Tiffani Ashley Bell
education: Howard University, BSc Systems and Computer Science
Stanford Graduate School of Business, MS Management (Sloan Fellow)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes her as a programmer and a 2017 Technology and Democracy Fellow at Harvard Kennedy School. Search snippets say Kristy Tillman co-created the Detroit Water Project in July 2014, but no opened page confirmed that, so she is not listed.

competitors.name: Detroit Water Fund (United Way backed assistance fund)
competitors.what: Public and philanthropic assistance fund for Detroit water bills, a substitute rather than a startup
competitors.traction_then: TechCrunch reports over 1,900 applicants qualified for the fund

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching and payment routing website with manual verification and direct payment to the water department; the hard parts were operational, not technical.

defensibility.rationale: Easy to copy as a website, but the early press attention and relationships with utilities gave some edge. Nonprofit status limits commercial moat questions.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it as a platform; the city's assistance fund ran alongside. The organization expanded to Baltimore by March 2015.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported about 33,000 Detroit residents had water cut off in 2014 and individual unpaid balances reaching several thousand dollars, which drew national press in summer 2014.

branding.domain_note: Main site remains detroitwaterproject.org per the YC listing and the site fetched in this research.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission led, human stories of individual donors and families on its blog

branding.brand_signature: The original Detroit Water Project name tied to the 2014 Detroit shutoff crisis

rebrands.why: Not stated in any source found; the YC page says the company was formerly the Detroit Water Project

branding.community_and_virality: The 2014 launch drew national coverage (TechCrunch, Marketplace, Nonprofit Quarterly) and the donor community grew to over 4,500 donors per its site.

brand_strength.rationale: The Detroit Water Project name earned wide press at launch; the later name is generic and the rename reason is unknown.

outcome_analysis: The Human Utility rode the 2014 Detroit water shutoff crisis, raising $170,000 for over 900 families by March 2015 and later reporting over 4,500 donors and 2,000 families helped. It stays active as a donation funded nonprofit, so venture style outcomes do not apply and no failure is evident.
notes: Dealroom lists two seed rounds of 120k and 125k with no investors or dates; single aggregator, unverified, not recorded as rounds. No outcome events found in searches. The company is a nonprofit so funding is mainly donations.
